source_text: Ἤπιά σοι πρὸς τοὺς ἀπαντῶντας ἔστω τὰ ῥήματα, καὶ προσηγορίαι γλυκεῖαι· αἰδὼς δὲ πρὸς γυναῖκας καὶ βλέμμα τετραμμένον εἰς γῆν. λάλει δὲ περιεσκεμμένως ἅπαντα, καὶ τῇ φωνῇ τὸ χρήσιμον ἀποδίδου, τῇ χρείᾳ τῶν ἀκουόντων τὸ φθέγμα μετρῶν, ἄχρι ἂν καὶ ἐξάκουστον ᾖ, καὶ μήτε διαφεῦγον τὴν ἀκοὴν τῶν παρόντων ὑπὸ σμικρότητος, μήτε ὑπερβάλλον μείζονι τῇ κραυγῇ. φυλάττου δὲ ὅπως μηδέν ποτε λαλήσῃς ὃ μὴ προεσκέψω καὶ προενόησας· μηδὲ προχείρως καὶ μεταξὺ τῶν τοῦ ἑτέρου λόγων ὑπόβαλλε τοὺς σαυτοῦ δεῖ γὰρ ἀνὰ μέρος ἀκούειν καὶ διαλέγεσθαι, χρόνῳ μερίζοντα λόγον καὶ σιωπήν· μάνθανε δὲ ἀσμένως, καὶ ἀφθόνως δίδασκε, μηδὲ ὑπὸ φθόνου ποτὲ σοφίαν ἀποκρύπτου πρὸς τοὺς ἑτέρους, μηδὲ μαθήσεως ἀφίστασο δι’ αἰδῶ. ὕπεικε πρεσβυτέροις ἴσα πατράσιν· τίμα θεράποντας θεοῦ· κάταρχε σοφίας καὶ ἀρετῆς. μηδὲ ἐριστικὸς ἔσο πρὸς τοὺς φίλους, μηδὲ χλευαστὴς κατ’ αὐτῶν καὶ γελωτοποιός· ψεῦδος δὲ καὶ δόλον καὶ ὕβριν ἰσχυρῶς παραίτου· σὺν εὐφημίᾳ δὲ φέρε καὶ τὸν ὑπερήφανον καὶ ὑβριστὴν ὡς πρᾷός τε καὶ μεγαλόψυχος ἀνήρ.
thought_title: Measured speech and modest bearing toward others
orientation: Clement continues his direct address to the newly baptized, giving practical rules for calm and modest speech and behavior toward other people.
pass_a_gloss: Let your words be gentle toward those you meet, and your greetings sweet; and let there be modesty toward women and a gaze turned to the ground. Speak all things with circumspection, and give back to your voice what is useful, measuring your utterance by the need of your hearers, until it is audible, and neither escaping the hearing of those present through smallness, nor exceeding with a greater shout. Guard yourself so that you never say anything which you have not examined beforehand and thought out beforehand; and do not rashly and in the middle of the other person's words interject your own. For it is necessary to hear and to converse in turn, dividing speech and silence by time. Learn gladly, and teach without envy, and never through envy hide wisdom from others, and do not stand away from learning through modesty. Yield to elders as to fathers; honor the servants of God; begin with wisdom and virtue. Do not be quarrelsome toward friends, nor a mocker against them and a jester; strongly refuse falsehood and deceit and insolence; and with graciousness bear both the proud man and the insolent man, as a gentle and great-souled man.

choices.why: Renders the adjective as a quality of speech, matching the context of words and greetings.
Uses the glossary English for αἰδώς, which the brief defines as modesty or reverence, especially toward women.
Captures the adverbial sense of careful, deliberate consideration in speaking.

choices.english: by the need of your hearers
choices.why: Keeps the dative of standard and the sense of measuring speech to what the audience requires.
rejected: according to the need of the listeners
to the use of those hearing

choices.why: Renders the verb's sense of throwing in one's own words while another is speaking.
Uses the glossary English for εὐφημία, defined as good speech or graciousness in bearing with the proud and insolent.

pass_b_english: Let your words to those you meet be gentle, and your greetings sweet. Show modesty toward women, and keep your gaze turned to the ground. Speak everything with circumspection, and give your voice what is useful, measuring your utterance by the need of your hearers, so that it is audible but does not escape the hearing of those present through being too small, nor exceed what is fitting with too loud a cry. Guard yourself so that you never say anything you have not examined and thought through beforehand. Do not rashly interject your own words in the middle of another person's speech, for you must listen and speak in turn, dividing speech and silence by time. Learn gladly, and teach without envy. Never hide wisdom from others out of jealousy, and do not withdraw from learning through modesty. Yield to elders as to fathers. Honor God's servants. Make a beginning with wisdom and virtue. Do not be quarrelsome toward your friends, nor mock them or play the buffoon at their expense. Strongly refuse falsehood, deceit, and insolence. Bear with the proud and insolent person with graciousness, as a gentle and great-souled man.

problems.quote: Take the lead in wisdom and virtue
problems.why: κάταρχε here means 'begin with' or 'make a start of,' not 'take the lead in.'
problems.fix: Make a beginning with wisdom and virtue.
problems.ruling: Greek verb κάταρχε = ‘begin/start’, not ‘lead’; translation changes instruction from ‘begin with wisdom and virtue’ to ‘take the lead in…’

edits.old: Take the lead in wisdom and virtue.
edits.new: Make a beginning with wisdom and virtue.

fixed: Changed 'Take the lead in wisdom and virtue' to 'Make a beginning with wisdom and virtue' because κάταρχε σοφίας καὶ ἀρετῆς means 'begin with wisdom and virtue,' not 'take the lead in.'
